subject: AWS + Azure multi-offer execution — private offer and marketplace billing playbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Hall <matthew.hall@aegislabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: AWS + Azure multi-offer execution — private offer and marketplace billing playbook

Hi Matthew,

Thanks again for the convo yesterday — excited to align on the renewal and the extra committed capacity you mentioned for Q4. Per our discussion, Aegis is planning to: (1) renew the base commitment and (2) add a 30% uplift that you'd like to split across AWS private offer (for prod workloads) and Azure Marketplace (for regional failover).

Attached is a draft mutual action plan and the PO stub you can use for procurement (Aegis_Renewal_MA-v2.docx; PO_Aegis_2026.pdf). Key asks so we can get this to DocuSign quickly:
- Confirm desired split: what % of the uplift should be on AWS PO vs Azure Marketplace (default suggestion: 70/30).
- Confirm preferred billing cadence for the Marketplace portion (monthly tranches vs quarterly invoice). We often do staggered marketplace invoices to match customer fiscal cadence — see billing-tranche-schedule.csv.
- Legal: any non-standard SOC or KMS notes we should expect in the SOW/PO?

If you confirm the split and cadence, we can trigger the AWS Private Offer creation and route the Azure Marketplace offer through Kimberly for marketplace invoicing and DocuSign. I copied Kimberly to handle the marketplace-side paperwork and Rishi to validate the SLA & acceptance window.

Proposed next steps:
1) You reply with split + billing cadence (EOD Thu).
2) We prepare PO + private offer and send DocuSign (target: <7 business days).
3) Procurement countersigns and we schedule onboarding ramp — Redwood will reserve the dedicated capacity once PO is received.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Renewals Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachments: Aegis_Renewal_MA-v2.docx, PO_Aegis_2026.pdf, billing-tranche-schedule.csv
From: Matthew Hall <matthew.hall@aegislabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aegis Labs Procurement <procurement@aegislabs.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@cloudbroker.io>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS + Azure multi-offer execution — private offer and marketplace billing playbook

Ben — thanks, this looks good.

We'd like to proceed. Quick replies:
- Split: we prefer 65% AWS private offer / 35% Azure Marketplace.
- Billing cadence: Azure Marketplace on monthly tranches tied to usage estimates (we need the ability to true-up quarterly).
- Legal: procurement wants a 60-day acceptance window instead of the standard 30, and to confirm that logs/audit retention align with our SOC 2 requirements.

I copied procurement — procurement@aegislabs.com — please loop them into any DocuSign flow. If you can send a detailed invoice tranche schedule and the final PO for signature, we'll push this through our internal approvals.

—Matt
Matthew Hall
Head of Platform Engineering | Aegis Labs
matthew.hall@aegislabs.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Hall <matthew.hall@aegislabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS + Azure multi-offer execution — private offer and marketplace billing playbook

Matt — perfect, thanks for the clarity.

Action plan (internal + external):

For Aegis (what we'll send to procurement):
- Final split: 65% AWS PO / 35% Azure Marketplace.
- Azure billing: monthly tranches with quarterly true-up; attached is an updated tranche schedule reflecting the 65/35 split (billing-tranche-schedule.csv).
- Acceptance window: we'll surface the 60-day request to Legal; Rishi, please confirm if Redwood can accept 60-day acceptance on this deal (SLA implications).

Internal tasks (owners):
- Kimberly: prepare Azure Marketplace offer and create the staged invoice plan. Please include a note that invoices will be issued monthly in tranches; finance will accept consolidated remittance to Aegis' billing contact. (Owner: kimberly_park)
- Rishi: review SLA/acceptance window and confirm if a 60-day acceptance is allowable for this account or if we need an SLA addendum. Also check implications for reserved capacity provisioning. (Owner: rishi_malhotra)
- Ben: I'll draft the DocuSign packet (PO + SOW + acceptance addendum if needed) and route to Matthew + procurement. Target send: Thu COB.

Notes for doc assembly: include explicit capacity ramp dates, rollback/fallback model variant (if backfill required), and a clear rollback clause for outstanding invoices. We want the AWS private offer to be created and approved in parallel with the Azure marketplace acceptance to avoid a provisioning gap.

Matt — one question: are there any constraints on invoice remit-to entity (e.g., Aegis US Holdings vs Aegis Labs EOS)? That will affect the marketplace invoicing flow.

Ben
Senior Renewals Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Matthew Hall <matthew.hall@aegislabs.com>, Aegis Labs Procurement <procurement@aegislabs.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS + Azure multi-offer execution — private offer and marketplace billing playbook

Ben / Rishi — looping back with the marketplace playbook and a couple of redline asks from Finance/Legal. I've attached the updated tranche CSV and a short marketplace checklist.

Marketplace notes / exceptions:
- We can support monthly tranches with quarterly true-ups. Finance requests that the Marketplace invoice P.O. reference include both the Private Offer reference and the Marketplace offer ID for reconciliation.
- Legal redline: acceptance window change to 60 days is acceptable for standard production SKUs but requires an SLA addendum for reserved capacity with a specified remediation timeline. Rishi, please confirm whether the SLA addendum template (SLA_Addendum_v1.docx) is acceptable or if Legal needs contract-level edits.
- Billing remit entity: procurement confirmed Aegis US Holdings is the remit-to; I've added that to the PO draft.

Next steps:
1) Ben: finalize DocuSign packet (I'll include the marketplace invoice schedule and marketplace offer ID fields).
2) Rishi: quick review of SLA_Addendum_v1.docx and call out any material changes (target: Fri EOB).
3) Matthew / Procurement: once DocuSign is sent, please confirm PO signature route (single signer vs two-step approval).

Attachments: billing-tranche-schedule.csv, SLA_Addendum_v1.docx

Thanks — I'll queue the Azure offer creation immediately after the DocuSign packet is live so there's no gap in provisioning.

—Kimberly Park
Manager, Cloud Marketplace Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
